projects.title: The Future of Gas Stations in the Context of Energy Transition
projects.html:
01 —Context

The rapid advancements in sustainable mobility and energy transition are reshaping the landscape of the fuel service station (EDS) industry globally, including in Colombia. This case study focuses on the current state and future prospects of gas stations in Colombia as they navigate through this significant transition. The initial context includes a network of approximately 6,000 gas stations, primarily operated by small and medium distributors, with major players like Terpel, Primax, Biomax, and Chevron dominating the market. The objective is to explore how these stations can evolve to meet the demands of a greener future.

02 —The Challenge

The primary challenge faced by the EDS industry in Colombia is the shift towards sustainable mobility amidst an environment still heavily reliant on fossil fuels. With a mere 0.2% of stations offering rapid charging for electric vehicles, the industry lags in infrastructure necessary for the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs). Key obstacles include convincing numerous small-scale station owners to invest in new technologies, developing a robust charging network, and addressing the low current demand for EVs. Additionally, the industry must align with global trends toward decarbonization and prepare for a market where electric and hybrid vehicles are expected to dominate.

03 —Methodology

I followed a structured process consisting of four key stages:

  1. Plan — Setup and Organization: This initial stage involves setting up the framework for the project, organizing the work schedule, and establishing objectives for the week. It ensures a clear roadmap and efficient time management for the exploration ahead.
  2. Explore — Desk Research, Trend Analysis and Expert Interviews: Conduct an extensive review of relevant documents and explore current trends. Interview two experts to gain insights and gather diverse perspectives.
  3. Define — Strategy Development: Based on the information gathered, define a strategic approach and identify key opportunity areas. This stage focuses on setting clear goals and outlining the potential impact of the proposed solutions.
  4. Imagine — Design Concept Projection: Develop and project various design concepts that address the identified opportunities. This creative stage involves brainstorming, sketching, and refining ideas to propose innovative and practical solutions.

04 —Results: Reimagining Service Stations

Various design concepts were developed to transform traditional gas stations into multifunctional centers adapted to sustainable mobility. These concepts include vehicular charging towers that optimize space, last-mile delivery hubs for urban areas, energy and experience centers that turn stations into recreational destinations, and home charging services for greater convenience. Additionally, charging station modules were proposed for high-traffic locations, multi-energy complexes on highways, workspaces known as "third places," and stations on green tourist routes. These designs aim to diversify services and energy offerings, enhance user experience, and support the transition to a more sustainable future.

05 —Intended Impact

Reimagining service stations results in significant benefits across multiple dimensions:

  • Environmental Impact: Shift to electric and renewable energy reduces carbon footprint; integration of solar panels and wind turbines supports sustainability.
  • Customer Experience: Introduction of EV charging, rental services, and experience centers; interactive and entertaining elements improve customer visits.
  • Economic Benefits: Services like EV rentals and home charging generate additional income; new services and technologies create employment opportunities.
  • Sustainable Mobility: Expanded network of EV chargers supports electric vehicle adoption; home charging services and public infrastructure alleviate EV range concerns.
  • Technological Advancements: Mobile apps for services and customer interaction enhance tech integration; efficient use of renewable energy sources.
  • Strategic Partnerships: Public-private partnerships foster sustainable mobility solutions; collaboration with startups and tech companies drives innovation.
  • Consumer Preferences: Data analytics provide customized services, enhancing satisfaction; green energy options meet environmentally conscious consumer expectations.
  • Business Viability: Diversification ensures long-term business viability; multiple energy and service options make stations more resilient to market changes.

01 —The Context

The Future Seeds building, part of the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT) in Palmira, Colombia, is a globally significant site for the conservation of agricultural biodiversity. Traditionally a space dedicated exclusively to scientific research, it held untapped potential to become a bridge between science and society. In partnership with Parque Explora, CIAT envisioned turning this emblematic space into a vibrant place where the public could understand and connect with the value of biodiversity and germplasm conservation.

02 —The Challenge

The main challenge was to transform underutilized areas of the Seeds of the Future building into engaging, educational spaces without interrupting its core scientific functions. The goal was to open the facility to diverse audiences while preserving its integrity as a research center—turning it into a dual-purpose environment that supports both rigorous science and compelling science communication.

03 —The Process

To initiate the transformation, we first established a close collaboration with CIAT’s scientific team to identify the core narratives that would resonate with both specialists and general visitors. These included the significance of preserving agricultural biodiversity, the role of germplasm in food security, and the global relevance of the Future Seeds facility. This dialogue allowed us to ground the design process in scientific accuracy while translating complex topics into accessible, meaningful stories.

With these narratives in place, we developed a design strategy rooted in the idea of “welcoming science.” This meant rethinking the way visitors move through the building and experience information. We identified underutilized zones within the facility that could be repurposed as interactive spaces without disrupting its operational flow. These zones became points of encounter—areas where the public could engage with content through immersive, sensory experiences.

We designed and installed three interactive exhibits that combined analog and digital elements. These exhibits invited visitors to explore seed diversity, conservation techniques, and the global exchange of agricultural knowledge. Each installation was carefully crafted to be intuitive, engaging, and visually compelling, using graphics, textures, and participatory components that would captivate both lay audiences and academic visitors.

The graphic and spatial interventions were designed to harmonize with the architectural and scientific context of the building. Rather than imposing a traditional museographic layer, we worked with the existing materiality and circulation of the space, embedding interpretive elements that felt natural and respectful of the building’s research identity.

Finally, we supported the integration of these new public functions by training CIAT scientists as science communicators and space mediators. Their presence and active participation enriched the visitor experience, allowing for real-time interpretation, dialogue, and connection. This human-centered approach helped bridge the gap between rigorous research and societal understanding, making the science come alive for everyone.

projects.title: Creating a Nationwide Network of Branches for the Museum of Natural and Cultural History of Colombia
projects.excerpt: Purpose. The project seeks to inspire a collective shift toward life-centered thinking, encouraging Colombians to explore the biodiversity of their territory and engage in its care. Through science, storytelling, and…
projects.html:
01 —The Context

In 2022, the Colombian Ministry of Culture launched a national initiative to create a network of spaces for the Museum of Natural and Cultural History of Colombia. The goal was to enhance public engagement with science and technology and spark a nationwide conversation centered on life, regeneration, and biodiversity. Through a public call, cultural, scientific, and educational institutions were invited to submit viable project proposals within just four weeks. Parque Explora, in collaboration with various partners, accepted the challenge to design and conceptualize the nationwide network.

02 —The Challenge

The main challenge was to develop a comprehensive and feasible proposal for 12 physical and 6 virtual museum spaces across Colombia in only four weeks. This demanded the coordination of multiple stakeholders, the crafting of a unified narrative that resonated nationwide, and the creation of adaptive content and formats that respected the diverse physical and social contexts of each location.

03 —The Idea

At its heart, the Network of spaces of the Museum of Natural and Cultural History of Colombia (MHNCC) is a call to recognize and celebrate the interconnections between life forms, ecosystems, and cultures across Colombia. The network was conceived not merely as a series of museum exhibitions, but as a national platform to regenerate our understanding and relationship with nature through knowledge, emotion, and action.

Purpose. The project seeks to inspire a collective shift toward life-centered thinking, encouraging Colombians to explore the biodiversity of their territory and engage in its care. Through science, storytelling, and design, Biofilia aims to spark ecological awareness and regenerative practices, rooted in local realities and ancestral knowledge.

04 —Content Approach

  • Anchor ourselves to a common history: Origin stories. Geological and cultural milestones that have created a changing and biodiverse territory.
  • Regenerate relationships and life: From a call for urgent action, it proposes the regeneration of soil, forests, and socio-ecological relationships.
  • Our present landscape: Who and how we live today in this shared territory. Stories about a present full of natural and cultural stories, around biodiversity and the challenges of resilience.

05 —Museography

We understood the spaces of the network as a large system made up of a set of interrelated museographic elements that take place in a specific physical and social context. Those elements can be grouped thematically, based on a single principle, a great idea, or a number of connections that make them coherent from an informative perspective.

Each exhibition is made up of a mixture of museographic formats, the result of both the resources available for the project, as well as the communicative and educational purposes of the MHNCC.

The modularity of formats

Each space in the network will have a mix of formats and their proportions adapted to the conceptual opportunities, institutional strengths, operational restrictions and experiences of the public. Thus, one space may have a more contemplative vocation, with a quick and self-managed visit, while another space may favor citizen participation and the collective construction of knowledge.

Space typologies

In order to achieve a flexible museum system that can be adapted to the different conditions of the network spaces, we considered two fundamental variables: the size of the space and its permanence over time. The crossing of the variables has allowed us to establish three types of spaces:

  • Space S (between 20 and 50 sqm)
  • Space M (between 50 and 100 sqm)
  • Space L (between 100 and 250 sqm)

Virtual spaces

A digital platform will be developed that will serve as a portal to disseminate content. It will also be the place where the public will be able to find resources of the e-Learning strategy.

06 —From Strategy to Impact

  • The network of spaces is now a reality known as Alianza Biofilia.
  • Successfully implemented a flexible museographic system that celebrates Colombia’s biological and cultural diversity.
  • Strengthened strategic partnerships and local capacities in science communication.
  • Enabled meaningful public engagement with science in historically underserved regions.
  • Achieved seamless integration between physical and digital museum formats.
  • Established the project as a benchmark for museum innovation and strategic design in Latin America.
  • Demonstrated the power of collaborative design in addressing complex challenges with national impact.

projects.title: Regenerative Horizons
projects.sub: Co-creating a Birds and Agriculture Park in Colombia
projects.html:
01 —Context

The Birds Park and Regenerative Agriculture project is located at Hacienda Piedechinche in El Cerrito, Valle del Cauca. This park aims to merge biodiversity conservation, particularly of birds, with regenerative agricultural practices, creating a space for sustainable learning and tourism. The initiative is a collaboration between Ingenio Providencia and Audubon Americas, with the goal of promoting environmental sustainability, education, and community integration.

02 —The Challenge

The main challenge of the project was to harmonize traditional agricultural production with biodiversity conservation, especially birds. The project needed to adapt regenerative agricultural practices while ensuring the protection and promotion of local bird species. There were specific difficulties in securing funding, ensuring public safety, and creating engaging experiences for diverse audiences. Moreover, integrating these practices within the existing cultural and historical context of the Hacienda added another layer of complexity.

03 —What We Did

  • Conducted site visits and strategic workshops.
  • Held interviews with key stakeholders including community leaders, environmental groups, and tourism experts.
  • Developed a co-creation and strategic thinking workshop to understand and project the vision of the park.
  • Mapped the territory to identify opportunities and challenges.
  • Collaborated with local universities and organizations to design and implement regenerative agricultural plots.
  • Integrated existing infrastructure with new sustainable architectural interventions.
  • Developed interactive and immersive experiences for visitors.
  • Designed digital strategies to maintain engagement with diverse audiences.

04 —The Master Plan

The master plan for the Birds Park and Regenerative Agriculture project successfully integrated various strategic components, creating a comprehensive framework that emphasizes environmental sustainability, education, and community engagement. It outlined the development of multiple thematic areas including contemplative spaces, regenerative scenarios, museographic settings, and experimental environments. The plan also incorporated existing infrastructure, ensuring ecological connectivity and modular, systemic design principles. Key results include the establishment of interactive and immersive visitor experiences, the creation of demonstration plots for regenerative agriculture, and the construction of innovative architectural spaces like elevated walkways, hides, and multi-purpose pavilions. 01 —The Situation

Artista de Archivo was originally an interactive installation housed at the Museo Cámara de Maravillas, part of the Biblioteca Pública Piloto in Medellín. Designed to engage visitors with archival content through creative composition tools, the exhibit invited users to remix visual fragments from Colombia’s cultural memory. With the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, the project faced a critical challenge: how to translate this hands-on museum experience into a meaningful and accessible digital interaction, at a time when cultural institutions were urgently seeking new strategies to stay connected with their audiences.

02 —The Task

I led the strategic and design adaptation of the experience, guiding its transition from a physical museum interface to an intuitive and engaging web platform. My responsibilities included experience mapping, UX/UI definition, usability validation, and the articulation of a communication strategy to ensure audience engagement in the digital space.

03 —The Process

The transformation process began with a co-creation workshop to identify what aspects of the original experience needed to be reinterpreted for digital environments. We established three pillars for adaptation: content simplification, interface redesign for responsive use, and usability optimization based on web heuristics. All graphic assets were reengineered for digital performance, and the user flow was redesigned as a step-by-step guided experience optimized for mobile.

We developed a functional prototype using Elementor within WordPress and conducted a System Usability Scale (SUS) test with 17 participants. Insights from these sessions led to key interface refinements and accessibility improvements.

Usability testing and iteration

The final experience allowed users to create custom compositions—letters, book covers, ex libris stamps—while integrating playful animations and social sharing features. Alongside, we developed a communications roadmap with campaigns and digital events to promote public engagement and creative participation.

04 —The Result

Artista de Archivo’s digital relaunch successfully extended the museum’s reach during a time of physical closure, while preserving its interactive and educational essence. The project strengthened the institution’s digital presence and set a precedent for hybrid cultural experiences. For me, it was a clear demonstration of how design can mobilize memory, creativity, and civic participation—even in times of disruption.

01 —Context

EUREKA Science Center is a proposed project aiming to establish a hub for culture, science, technology, and innovation in Cúcuta, Colombia, and the colombo-venezuelan border region. The project seeks to enhance scientific literacy, cultural enrichment, and community development, thereby transforming the local socio-economic landscape.

02 —The Challenge

The primary challenge was to design a master plan that addresses the socio-cultural and logistical complexities of the border region. The project needed to:

  • Understand and integrate the needs and aspirations of the community.
  • Ensure the center's design and activities are relevant and engaging.
  • Align with existing urban and regional development plans.
  • Foster cross-border collaboration and integration.

We conducted a comprehensive master planning process for the EUREKA Science Center, involving a strategic thinking workshop with local leaders and community members, detailed surveys, and in-depth user interviews to gather insights on community expectations and needs. We analyzed over 24 existing documents to extract relevant data, conducted more than 25 stakeholder interviews to identify opportunities, and produced key strategic deliverables, including a Diagnosis, and a final Definition Report. Additionally, we performed a contextual and spatial analysis to ensure the center's design aligns with regional frameworks and community needs.

The project defined architectural and design strategies to create an inviting, functional, and educational space. It also outlined the ASCTI program for operational models, emphasizing sustainability and autonomous management. The center aims to promote cultural diversity, social inclusion, and community engagement. Conceptually, EUREKA embraces the idea of a "diffuse frontier" as a zone of transition, a "context expanded" to connect local and global perspectives, an "environmental identity" recognizing humans as part of the ecosystem, and "open knowledge" merging traditional sciences with art and culture. Thematically, it covers intelligent life, culture, ecology, environment, science, and technology. Spatially, EUREKA is designed to be permeable, adaptable, expanded, progressive, and affective, integrating with the environment and fostering community involvement.

projects.title: Strategic Transformation of Parque Explora Amidst Covid Crisis

01 —The Context

In response to the unprecedented challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, Parque Explora initiated a strategic transformation process called "Compás Estratégico" in 2020. This initiative aimed to reimagine the organization’s role and operations during a time of crisis, with a focus on addressing societal challenges, adapting to new realities, and ensuring long-term sustainability. Through collaborative sessions, the organization sought to redefine its purpose, identify critical priorities, and prepare for various future scenarios while maintaining its mission of fostering education, culture, and science.

02 —The Challenge

The pandemic brought significant disruptions, including reduced cultural tourism, financial instability, and heightened social inequalities. Parque Explora faced declining revenues from ticket sales and partnerships, limited physical engagement with audiences, and the need to adapt quickly to digital platforms. Additionally, the organization had to address internal challenges such as breaking down silos, fostering collaboration, and building resilience to navigate an uncertain future effectively.

03 —The Process

The transformation process was structured into three strategic thinking sessions: defining a narrative of purpose, envisioning a reimagined future, and identifying actionable strategies. Using iterative cycles of learning and adaptation, the team explored potential scenarios—ranging from prolonged economic contraction to rapid recovery—and their implications for the organization. Key activities included mapping organizational capabilities, aligning resources to emerging opportunities, and developing a roadmap for agility and resilience. The sessions emphasized collaboration, creativity, and systemic thinking to ensure alignment with Parque Explora’s mission and adaptability to evolving conditions.

04 —The Impact

The "Compás Estratégico" initiative resulted in a clear framework of five strategic priorities: enhancing community impact, consolidating a transmedia ecosystem, strengthening alliances for sustainability, identifying critical resources and capacities, and becoming a more agile and resilient organization. These priorities were supported by actionable goals, such as expanding digital offerings, fostering inclusivity, and improving operational flexibility. The process also highlighted the importance of leveraging technology, forming new partnerships, and addressing barriers like resistance to change. By preparing for multiple scenarios, Parque Explora positioned itself to navigate uncertainty while reinforcing its role as a leader in education, culture, and science.

Strengthening Public Science Infrastructure in Valle del Cauca, Colombia

01 —Situation — The Challenge

After more than a decade of operation, two major science centers in Valle del Cauca—the Museo de Historia Natural y Cultural del Valle del Cauca (operated by INCIVA) and the Museo Interactivo Abracadabra (operated by the Departmental Library)—were facing declining relevance. Their museography had become outdated, technical infrastructure was obsolete, and educational content no longer reflected contemporary scientific narratives. Although both institutions shared the same public complex, La Manzana del Saber, their experiences were fragmented architecturally, operationally, and organizationally. This fragmentation weakened collaboration, governance, and the overall visitor experience at a time when Colciencias (now MinCiencias) was prioritizing the strengthening of science centers nationwide.

02 —Task — My Role

I served as one of the project’s strategic design leads, helping articulate a shared vision across both institutions and aligning diverse stakeholders around a unified experience model. I worked closely with institutional directors, curatorial teams, educators, architects, and public-sector partners to frame the challenge holistically. My responsibility spanned strategic framing, experience visioning, and methodological leadership across education, infrastructure, governance, and content. I also played a key role in orchestrating large-scale, parallel workstreams to ensure coherence across disciplines.

03 —Action — The Process

Diagnostic & Baseline Definition. We began with a comprehensive 360° diagnostic phase to establish a shared understanding of the current state. This included assessing museography, educational models, physical and technical infrastructure, organizational collaboration, and governance structures. This evidence-based baseline became the foundation for all subsequent decisions.

Unified Experience & Strategic Alignment. Through workshops and co-creation sessions, we aligned both institutions around the idea of a single, integrated science center experience—later named MALVA. This required reframing the project beyond exhibition design to include learning models, operational collaboration, and long-term governance.

Concurrent Design & Content Development. With a multidisciplinary team of over 30 professionals working in parallel, we developed museographic formats, architectural concepts, mediation strategies, and scientific narratives. New content areas included Earth and space sciences, biodiversity, experimentation zones, and public creative laboratories, all designed to foster participation and intergenerational learning.

Governance & Sustainability Model. In parallel, we defined a new collaboration and governance model to enable sustained coordination between institutions. This ensured that the unified experience was supported not only by design, but by organizational and strategic structures capable of maintaining it over time.

04 —Result — The Impact

MALVA became a fully designed and largely implemented integrated science center, successfully unifying two previously fragmented institutions into a coherent public experience. The project refreshed scientific narratives, modernized infrastructure, and introduced more participatory, family-oriented, and inclusive ways of engaging with science. Beyond physical transformation, MALVA enabled stronger institutional collaboration and positioned La Manzana del Saber as a contemporary, future-facing science and learning ecosystem—demonstrating how strategic design can drive long-term public value.

01 —Situation

The Panama Canal Authority sought to deepen national understanding of the Canal’s historic, ecological, and geopolitical significance—particularly among inland communities historically disconnected from it. To achieve this, they launched a competition to conceptualize a new interactive visitor center in Santiago de Veraguas, a region strategically selected for its location at the country’s center. The challenge: make the Canal’s global relevance and local impact tangible, participatory, and meaningful for all Panamanians.

02 —Task

As Senior Exhibit Designer within the Parque Explora team, I played a key role in shaping the conceptual vision and interactive storytelling strategy for the proposal. I focused on aligning spatial narratives with community engagement goals, ensuring that design decisions resonated with diverse audiences and communicated the Canal’s value beyond its economic function. My contributions spanned from early ideation to concept development, integrating participatory research and interpretive planning throughout.

03 —Action

We approached the project as both a spatial and cultural bridge, creating a visitor journey that invites people to feel like they are inside the Canal. The concept featured six themed galleries and 18 interactive experiences, combining analog, digital, and hybrid media.

Visitors could explore the geological origins of the isthmus, the biodiversity of its ecosystems, and the engineering milestones of the Canal’s construction and expansion. To develop locally grounded content, we conducted participatory field research in the region and used co-creation methodologies to surface community perspectives.

This informed the center’s tone, media formats, and modes of interaction. Through immersive storytelling, we translated complex themes—like geopolitics, water management, and global trade—into engaging, accessible formats for all ages.

04 —Result

Our proposal won the national competition, initiating the detailed design phase for the Panama Canal Experience Center. The project succeeded in reframing the Canal not just as infrastructure, but as a living symbol of national identity and shared responsibility. This case reaffirmed the power of inclusive design practices to foster public engagement and instill a sense of ownership over large-scale heritage narratives.

Usamos diversos formatos digitales, análogos y mixtos. Asimismo, nuestra metodología de investigación en campo nos permitió abordar el conocimiento de manera participativa. En este lugar, los visitantes reconocen esta gran obra de la humanidad.

projects.html:
01 —Situation

The El Niño and La Niña climate phenomena are often explained through scientific or technical lenses, focusing on meteorological complexity and global impact. However, this project sought to surface the sociocultural dimensions that are often overlooked: how communities experience, narrate, and make sense of these shifts. In collaboration with Parque Explora (Colombia), the Cité de l’espace, and the Toulouse Museum (France), we co-created an exhibition that reframes these phenomena through the lived experiences of people. The goal was to provoke reflection, empathy, and dialogue by bringing art and science into a shared, sensorial space.

02 —Task

I led the conceptualization and experience design of the exhibition, guiding the curatorial direction alongside scientific and cultural institutions in Colombia and France. I collaborated closely with content experts, museographers, and exhibition producers to shape a compelling, participatory narrative. My role spanned from early framing and narrative design to the creative supervision of the final visitor experience across multiple geographies. This project allowed me to push boundaries in how climate phenomena can be communicated through sociocultural storytelling.

03 —Action

Concept Development. We began by defining a unifying metaphor for the exhibition: overlapping stories. Inspired by the duality of El Niño and La Niña, we explored the tensions between dry and wet seasons, abundance and scarcity, personal and collective memory. These polarities informed the thematic and spatial structure of the exhibition. We developed a multi-sensory narrative strategy using color filters as an interpretive device, enabling visitors to shift perspectives physically and metaphorically.

Co-Design & Content Curation. In collaboration with scientists, educators, and community representatives, we gathered stories and materials that reflected diverse sociocultural impacts of the phenomena. This included testimonies, local artifacts, soundscapes, and visual media. Working with international partners enriched the scope of narratives and helped validate content across contexts.

Exhibition Design & Production. We designed three thematic spaces that could evoke emotional and intellectual engagement. Each space invited visitors to navigate overlapping timelines, geographies, and personal experiences. The exhibition blurred the line between art and science through immersive visuals, interactive components, and contrasting atmospheres. Despite limited resources, we prototyped several installation formats to test audience response before full-scale production.

International Launch & Adaptation. Following its initial run in Medellín, the exhibition was adapted and installed in France and Mexico. Each iteration maintained the core concept but was locally contextualized to reflect relevant stories and cultural references. The traveling nature of the exhibition enabled cross-cultural exchange and increased its reach and resonance.

04 —Result

The exhibition successfully shifted public understanding of El Niño and La Niña from abstract climate events to deeply human, context-rich experiences. It sparked meaningful engagement across age groups and cultural backgrounds, increasing awareness of environmental vulnerability and resilience.

A key learning was the power of metaphor and multisensory design to create emotional and cognitive access to complex phenomena. Though modest in scale, the project positioned us as experimental leaders in international museographic storytelling and strengthened institutional ties across Latin America and Europe.

Allies: Cité de l'espace, Embajada de Francia en Colombia, Instituto Francés.

projects.title: Claustro San Ignacio
projects.sub: Strategic Master Plan for Cultural Transformation
projects.excerpt: Strategic Framing & Intention Setting. Applying Parque Explora’s VEA (Visión de la Experiencia de Aprendizaje) methodology, we co-created a Manifiesto de Intención articulating a shared vision: to convert the Claustro…
projects.html:
01 —Situation

Since 2003, Comfama, a Colombian social enterprise, has operated the historic Claustro San Ignacio in Medellín primarily as a service center and educational facility. Recognizing its underutilization and immense cultural potential, Comfama partnered with Parque Explora to reimagine the building as a leading cultural and creative hub. This project aimed to honor the site's architectural heritage while transforming it into a space that fosters human development, citizenship, and inclusive cultural expression.

02 —The Challenge

The building’s use was predominantly transactional, centered around a client service model that deterred public engagement. Key architectural features like patios, the chapel (auditorium), and the library were either inaccessible or inadequately equipped to support meaningful cultural and educational experiences. Spatial disconnects, and limited accessibility further highlighted the need for a radical transformation aligned with contemporary urban and cultural dynamics.

03 —Task

I was part of the core team that supported Comfama and Parque Explora in defining the foundational vision and strategic direction for the Claustro’s transformation. My role spanned design research, synthesis, creative facilitation, and conceptual development, helping to co-create the manifesto, spatial strategy, and cultural positioning of the project. I collaborated closely with internal Comfama leaders, service teams, architects, and educators to shape a shared vision grounded in user needs and institutional purpose.

04 —Action

Discovery & Alignment. We conducted site visits, stakeholder interviews, and participatory workshops with over a dozen Comfama leaders across service, education, infrastructure, and strategy. This groundwork surfaced critical tensions: the mismatch between the building’s potential and its current usage, and the need for a more welcoming, inspiring, and inclusive civic space.

Strategic Framing & Intention Setting. Applying Parque Explora’s VEA (Visión de la Experiencia de Aprendizaje) methodology, we co-created a Manifiesto de Intención articulating a shared vision: to convert the Claustro into a creative center for talent development and cultural activation. We defined foundational principles—participation, critical thinking, inspiration, and expression—and mapped their implications for content, experience, and space.

Conceptual Design & Spatial Strategy. We proposed a new architectural and programmatic schema that transformed the Claustro from a service-heavy, closed-off building into a layered public environment. The plan introduced flexible learning labs, exhibition zones, cultural stages, and a public rooftop terrace. Space typologies included a transmedia lab, gastronomy studio, ideation workshops, and a reimagined Comfama Interactivo hub.

Roadmap & Feasibility. Finally, we detailed a phased transformation plan including architectural programs, intervention stages, budget projections, and operational strategy to enable ongoing learning and adaptation through execution.

Process Highlights

  • Conducted site visits, stakeholder interviews, and co-creation workshops to capture insights and aspirations.
  • Applied the VEA (Learning Experience Vision) methodology for systemic and user-centered design.
  • Defined a strategic vision and architectural program aligned with Comfama’s mission and community needs.
  • Proposed a multifunctional layout including public plazas, creative labs, coworking areas, and reimagined learning spaces.
  • Designed flexible environments such as the Transmedia Lab, Gastronomy Lab, and Public Auditorium to support diverse cultural programming.
  • Created accessibility improvements and integrated vertical circulation systems to unify the building experience.
  • Developed a phased execution plan to allow continuous operation during the renovation.

05 —Result

This work established the strategic and experiential foundation for one of Medellín’s most ambitious civic transformations. The Claustro has since evolved into a reference point for cultural life in the city, with over 2.1 million visitors and 6,000+ public events hosted between 2023 and 2025. The project demonstrated how heritage spaces can be reactivated through purpose-driven design, and it shaped my ongoing approach to aligning physical transformation with institutional vision and user meaning.

projects.html:
01 —Situation

The temporary exhibition Molas: Layers of Wisdom at the Gold Museum of Bogotá sought to reveal the worldviews and ancestral knowledge of the Guna people from Colombia and Panama. Central to this cultural expression are the molas—multi-layered textiles worn by Guna women, rich in symbolic and protective meaning. The curatorial challenge was to transform these intricate fabrics into an immersive sensory experience that could communicate the spiritual journey of the Neles (Guna leaders and visionaries), honoring their layered cosmogonies and connection to the creative forces of the world.

02 —Task

I was responsible for leading the conceptualization and audiovisual design of the immersive piece Los Galus. My task was to translate Guna cosmology into a spatial narrative that could evoke the dreamlike journeys of the Neles through the layered dimensions of the molas. The objective was not to represent their stories literally, but to create a respectful, affective space of contemplation and wonder.

03 —Action

We designed Los Galus as an immersive room experience where visitors entered a liminal space of overlapping visuals, textures, and sounds—mirroring the layered textile logic of the molas. Inspired by the idea of crossing thresholds between spiritual realms, the installation used projection mapping, ambient soundscapes, and mirrored surfaces to generate a sense of infinite space and symbolic depth.

Our team collaborated with anthropologists, curators, and Guna advisors to ensure cultural accuracy and sensitivity. The narrative structure avoided linear storytelling, favoring an open, sensorial rhythm that echoed the dreamlike sequences described by the Neles. The visual language was based on abstract forms drawn from traditional mola iconography, unfolding in cycles to simulate ritual and reverie. We complemented this with La Mujer y la Mola, a second audiovisual experience focused on the wisdom of Guna women and the act of creation.

04 —Result

The exhibition offered museum visitors a profound and contemplative experience—one that moved beyond explanation into immersion. Los Galus became a highlight of the show, praised for its poetic interpretation of Guna cosmology. The project reaffirmed how immersive media can honor indigenous narratives by embracing ambiguity, symbolism, and emotional resonance over didactic formats.

projects.html:
01 —Situation

As Colombia deepened its national strategy for inclusive science, technology, and innovation, there was a growing need to guide the creation and strengthening of Science Centers across the country. Backed by Colciencias and developed in partnership with Parque Explora, this national guide aimed to align new and existing centers with global benchmarks for fourth- and fifth-generation institutions—spaces focused on experiential learning, public engagement, and citizen participation in science and technology. The challenge was to translate these ambitions into practical, scalable guidance.

02 —Task

I served as co-author of the guide, leading the interior design and learning environments component. My responsibility was to define the spatial and experiential principles that would help Science Centers move beyond exhibition toward becoming participatory, educational ecosystems. I collaborated closely with museologists, architectural and technical design experts, and specialists in public engagement to integrate pedagogical intent into the spatial logic of these centers.

03 —Action

Conceptual Design of Spatial Guidelines. We began by analyzing global models (ASTC, ECSITE, RedPOP) and emerging trends such as public engagement with science and technology. These informed a set of spatial design principles grounded in flexibility, multi-sensory interaction, accessibility, and inclusive design—translating educational values into physical environments.

Guide Development and Field Validation. Working in tandem with Parque Explora’s Design and curatorial teams, we structured the guide into thematic routes. My contribution focused on the Interior Design and Learning Environments sections, aligning physical layouts with informal, participatory learning practices. The design principles were positioned as tools to shape not just space, but behavior and engagement within it.

Pilot Application: Project Malva. The guidelines were tested in the strengthening of two Science Centers in Valle del Cauca, as part of the Malva project. This served as a live pilot to assess how spatial design influenced the learning experience and community ownership of the centers.

04 —Result

The guide established a shared national framework for designing next-generation Science Centers in Colombia. Its adoption has helped elevate the quality and coherence of projects nationwide—bridging physical design with educational mission. A key learning was the value of integrating spatial and pedagogical thinking early in the process to ensure spaces not only function, but transform how people relate to science and each other.

Scalability and National Adoption. Since publication, the guide has become a national reference. It was instrumental in shaping the vision and spatial strategies of the CIBI Science Center in Dosquebradas and used as a diagnostic and planning tool in the Science Center of the Technological University of Pereira. Many more initiatives across the country continue to draw from its framework.

MOVA is the innovation center for teachers in Medellín. We conceptualized this novel environment as the intersection of three dimensions: being, knowing, and creating; which makes it possible to develop and nurture personal and professional skills aimed at the generation of educational experiences, with diverse and contextualized pedagogical practices, based on dialogue and the exchange of ideas and experiences.

Learning by doing and teaching by showing is a common methodological commitment that is defined in spatial relationships and ways of inhabiting the project. Criteria such as spatial simultaneity, gaps and transparencies, and the mix of activities allow the generation of more complex relationships by giving visibility to all the experiences that take place, finding a fertile environment for creation.

01 —Minor stories

Minor stories is an interactive exhibit equipped with a tangible interface using a mapping projection technique on a relief table.

An aboriginal community on an island is created, where plants, animals, villagers and a shaman who prays to the heavens when facing an intense summer or a harsh winter. The visitors share complete control of the situation, moving and rotating tags around the projected surface. Handling said objects, the visitors can create different situations: they may change the day into night, summer into winter, create bird and UFO effects, and even inflict natural disasters on specific regions.

  • Sensory Engagement: The video projection on a relief surface surprises the visitor, who also finds himself with some objects that allow him to interact with the game in a new and tangible manner.
  • Creative Engagement: Each visitor is invited to experiment and create their own short story.
  • Social Engagement: Three people may simultaneously share the experience and observe the results.

projects.html:
01 —Situation

Parque Explora sought to renew one of its most iconic galleries: Sala Mente (The Mind Gallery). Originally developed in 2011 in collaboration with the Neuroscience Group of the University of Antioquia, the gallery needed to evolve into a more engaging, inclusive, and contemporary experience. The aim was to translate cutting-edge brain research into an interactive and emotional learning environment—one that would stimulate curiosity, imagination, and self-reflection for all audiences.

02 —Task

I was responsible for the interactive design of the gallery. My role covered the end-to-end development of visitor experiences: from concept and interaction logic to technical detailing, prototyping, and coordinating production and installation. I worked closely with scientists, exhibit fabricators, and Explora’s internal team to ensure each component was both scientifically accurate and emotionally resonant.

03 —Action

Collaborative Research & Concept Framing. The foundation of the project was a close partnership with neuroscientists from the University of Antioquia. We held regular working sessions to translate complex research into clear, relatable narratives. This collaboration ensured that each exhibit spoke to everyday experiences, while remaining grounded in scientific rigor.

Interaction & Experience Design. We reimagined the gallery not as a static display, but as a “moving medium” for dialogue. Instead of organizing content by brain anatomy, we structured the space around human abilities—like dreaming, sensing, imagining, and communicating—making the subject matter more accessible and emotionally resonant.

Exhibition Architecture & Thematic Zones. The space was divided using a color-coded system, with each zone inviting exploration of different cognitive functions. Every interaction was designed to be intuitive and open-ended, encouraging visitors to test their memory, perception, or creativity at their own pace. The gallery was built around a free-choice learning model, allowing for nonlinear exploration and playful experimentation.

Prototyping, Detailing & Installation. I led the technical detailing and production coordination for the interactive stations—ensuring that each piece could withstand heavy public use while maintaining fidelity to the intended experience. This included mechanical exhibits, digital interfaces, physical triggers, and sensor-based interactions. I also oversaw the final assembly and installation on-site.

04 —Result

Sala Mente became one of the most beloved spaces in Parque Explora, praised for its ability to spark wonder and self-inquiry. The gallery successfully bridged the gap between neuroscience and everyday life, turning abstract concepts into tangible, joyful, and sometimes surreal experiences. A key learning: designing for the mind requires engaging both the intellect and the body—offering not just information, but opportunities to feel, imagine, and question.

home.bio: Director de Diseño Estratégico y Transformación de CX con más de 15 años construyendo las condiciones para que las organizaciones naveguen la complejidad, rediseñen cómo operan y creen valor a largo plazo. Lidero en la intersección de la prospectiva, el pensamiento sistémico y el diseño centrado en las personas, traduciendo la ambigüedad estratégica en nuevos modelos operativos, ecosistemas digitales y capacidades organizacionales. Mi trabajo abarca energía, servicios financieros, retail y sector público en América Latina.

approach.lead: Todo proyecto empieza con una pregunta, no con una solución. Mi práctica se apoya en seis principios que guían cómo trabajo con organizaciones que enfrentan complejidad estratégica — desde replantear el problema correcto hasta diseñar las condiciones para un cambio duradero.
principles: Destilo ideas complejas en narrativas claras y enfocadas que inspiran acción y transformación. A través de la narración conecto profundamente con las audiencias e impulso el cambio haciendo lo esencial visible y memorable.

Entiendo el diseño como un proceso compartido: trabajo de cerca con las comunidades para construir soluciones arraigadas en sus realidades. Este enfoque inclusivo produce resultados más significativos, sostenibles y aceptados.

Desde el pensamiento sistémico diseño con conciencia del contexto más amplio, conectando las dinámicas organizacionales, las necesidades de las personas y las fuerzas sociales para lograr un impacto duradero y sistémico.
Ayudo a las organizaciones a mirar más allá del presente, diseñando soluciones preparadas para el futuro que construyen resiliencia y aseguran relevancia en un mundo en constante cambio.
A través del prototipado rápido y las pruebas iterativas, convierto ideas en soluciones validadas con rapidez, acelerando el aprendizaje, la adaptación y una innovación medible.
Diseño de marcos a la medida

Diseño estrategias a la medida del reto, no plantillas. Al replantear los problemas e integrar un pensamiento sistémico y centrado en las personas, abro soluciones significativas y ajustadas al contexto.

about.intro: Soy Director de Diseño Estratégico y Transformación, con más de 15 años construyendo las condiciones para que las organizaciones naveguen la complejidad, reimaginen cómo operan y creen valor a largo plazo. Mi práctica se ubica en la intersección de la prospectiva, el pensamiento sistémico, el diseño de servicios y la cocreación centrada en las personas — traduciendo la ambigüedad estratégica en marcos accionables, nuevos modelos operativos y capacidades organizacionales que perduran.
about.quote: Creo que la complejidad no es un problema por resolver — es una condición que hay que navegar. Las organizaciones con las que trabajo no necesitan respuestas más simples. Necesitan mejores preguntas, modelos más claros y la capacidad organizacional de actuar con intención en la incertidumbre.
experience: Como líder de Diseño Estratégico y CX y hoy Director de Consultoría en VML Colombia, he liderado proyectos de transformación de principio a fin para organizaciones en puntos de inflexión estratégica. Mi trabajo abarca el diseño de modelos de prospectiva, la estrategia de ecosistemas digitales, el rediseño de modelos operativos y la innovación en experiencia de cliente — siempre en la intersección entre el rigor del diseño y el pragmatismo del negocio. Actualmente lidero el Centro de Excelencia de Consultoría para LATAM, escalando nuestra práctica de diseño estratégico en Colombia, México, Perú, Chile y Puerto Rico.

Durante más de 11 años en Parque Explora construí mi práctica desde cero — empecé como diseñador de exposiciones y llegué a ser Jefe de Innovación. Lideré los proyectos de transformación más ambiciosos de la institución: la renovación completa de un centro de ciencia, el diseño de entornos de aprendizaje inmersivos para clientes nacionales e internacionales y el desarrollo de la metodología de innovación de Parque Explora, publicada como Compás de Diseño. El trabajo de esta etapa recibió reconocimiento de la American Alliance of Museums (Muse Awards 2017) y de la Bienal Iberoamericana de Diseño en Madrid.
